Notes:
- Our classification tiers: IDENTIFIER (email, phone), SENSITIVE_ATTR (health flags/diagnosis), INFERRED_HEALTH (model-derived risk signals). We treat telemetry logs containing raw text as transient: stored encrypted at rest, default retention 30 days for non-support telemetry, 90 days for debug captures with explicit consent.
- Pseudonymization approach: we tokenize identifiers and apply reversible tokenization only when customer requests data retrieval; otherwise one-way hashing plus salt per-customer. For PHI in free text we prefer structured extraction + pseudonymize tokens; full redaction is used when retention is unnecessary.
- KMS scoping: per-tenant keys for Dedicated/Private; hosted tenants use a shared key ring with per-tenant envelope keys. Only Security Ops + SRE on-call have key rotation privileges (least-privilege).

Hannah — can you confirm region exclusions for health datasets (we currently avoid eu-west-3 for some health workloads; full matrix in your diagram).

Hi Elena / Sergei,

Thanks for the clear list. Attached are consolidated artifacts and short answers to the bullets in your SSQ:

Attachments included (stubs):
- redwood-role-based-access-playbook.pdf (playbook: role scenarios, least-privilege rules, and reviewer checklist)
- redwood-dataflow-diagram-v2.png (annotated dataflow showing where raw inputs may touch systems, pseudonymization points, and telemetry stores)
- kms-attestation-redwood-2028-08.pdf (key custody and rotation attestation)
- export-playbook-redwood-2028-08.md (how we produce exports and scrub PIAs)

Short answers (high level):
1) Classification & treatment: IDENTIFIER, SENSITIVE_ATTR, INFERRED_HEALTH (see playbook pp. 2–3). Raw user text is treated as transient; default telemetry retention is 30 days unless debug retention is requested (90 days) and authorized by the customer.

2) Role-based access:
- Support Agents / CS: access to de-identified transcripts and structured metadata only.
- Security Ops / SRE: access to encrypted raw logs for debugging; access requires Just-In-Time approval and is audited.
- Research/Modeling: access only to pseudonymized or synthetic datasets — no raw PHI.

3) Pseudonymization vs. Redaction:
- Preferred: structured extraction + reversible tokenization only under customer request.
- Default: non-reversible hashing + salt per-tenant for identifiers when retention is needed for analytics.
- Redaction used when retention provides no value or policy requires removal.

4) Cross-border / jurisdictional handling:
- We limit inference and log persistence for customer-designated "health" workloads to regions listed in the diagram. For BlueWell we recommend EU keys and processing in eu-west-1 or us-east-1 with contractual controls; full routing policy available in the attached diagram.

If you need deeper evidence (audit trace export or per-request headers for a sample timeframe) we can run a sanitized export; Marissa has attached the export playbook and KMS attestation for your review.
